title: [Chapitre] VIII. Analysis situs (quatrième mouture) : notes manuscrites (26/06-04/07/1986).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting (from pp. 37-40). A set |Φ| (the underlying set of a 'figure') is covered by a family (X_i)_{i∈I} of subsets indexed by an ordered set I. For x in |Φ|, let I^x = {i : x ∈ X_i}. The 'open stratum' is X_i° = X_i minus the union of the X_j for j<i, i.e. the set of x for which i is minimal in I^x. Let I' = {i : X_i° ≠ ∅}.

The conditions being compared:
- (i): every I^x has a smallest element.
- (ii): (2') the X_i° are pairwise disjoint, and (3') X_i = ∪_{j≤i} X_j°.
- (iv): α) the X_i° (i∈I') partition |Φ|; β) each X_i is saturated for that partition; γ) if X_j° ≠ ∅ and X_j° ⊂ X_i, then j ≤ i.

The previous page proved (i) ⇔ 2') + 3') = (ii).

On this page Grothendieck translates (iv) into the same language:
- 1'') covering; this is 1').
- 2'') saturation: X_i = ∪_{j∈I'(i)} X_j°, where I'(i) = {j∈I' : X_j° ⊂ X_i}.
- 3'') γ rewritten as I'(i) = I' ∩ I_{≤i}. Since X_j° = ∅ off I', this gives ∪_{I'(i)} X_j° = ∪_{j≤i} X_j°.

Given 3''), 2'') becomes 3'). Hence (iv) ⇔ 1') + 2') + 3') + γ ⇔ (i) + γ. So (iv) ⇔ (i) reduces to showing (i) ⇒ γ. This follows from Corollary 1: under (i)/(ii), for X_j° ≠ ∅,
j ≤ i ⇔ X_j ⊂ X_i ⇔ X_j° ⊂ X_i ⇔ X_j° ∩ X_i ≠ ∅.

The proof starts from 3'): X_i = ∪_{i'≤i} X_{i'}°, hence i ≤ j ⇒ X_i ⊂ X_j. It is finished on p. 40 using the partition property.

A side remark ('NB ... ?!') notes that the proposition never assumed monotonicity i ≤ j ⇒ X_i ⊂ X_j. A margin note explains why the hypothesis X_j° ≠ ∅ is needed in γ: the empty set is contained in every X_i.

Modern reading: (i) says exactly that there is a map s: |Φ| → I, s(x) = min I^x, with X_i = s^{-1}(I_{≤i}). In other words, the family is the pullback along a map to I of the principal down-sets, i.e. a set-level poset-stratification. Corollary 2 (p. 40) says that if all strata are nonempty, i ↦ X_i is an order embedding (a 'rigid figure'). This is an elementary foundational lemma for the stratified 'analysis situs' (tame topology) project.
errors: Gap/circularity concerning monotonicity. The translation of condition 3°) (p. 38) only gives the inclusion X_i ⊂ ∪_{j≤i} X_j°. The reverse inclusion, and so the equality 3'), needs i ≤ j ⇒ X_i ⊂ X_j, which is not assumed. Yet the proof of Corollary 1 derives monotonicity from 3'). Counterexample without monotonicity: I = {a<b}, X_a = {p}, X_b = {q}. Then (i) and (iv) hold, but 3') fails (∪_{j≤b} X_j° = {p,q}) and a ≤ b does not give X_a ⊂ X_b. Grothendieck's own 'NB ... ?!' flags exactly this. The fix is to assume the family is monotone (a functor I → P(|Φ|)), as a figure indexed by an ordered set presumably is.
In the list of conditions he writes '∀ i,j ∈ I, X_i° ∩ X_j° = ∅' without the needed 'i ≠ j' (a slip; 2') on p. 38 has it).
The step 'compte tenu de 3''), 2'') équivaut à ...' is left syntactically unfinished, though the intended conclusion (2'') ⇔ 3')) is clear.

ideas.what: Characterizing when a poset-indexed covering family of subsets comes from a stratification: every point has a smallest index containing it, iff the strata X_i° = X_i minus ∪_{j<i} X_j are disjoint and X_i = ∪_{j≤i} X_j°.
ideas.modern_name: Poset-stratification as a map X → I (to I with its Alexandrov topology); closed strata as preimages of down-sets
ideas.usually_credited_to: Folklore; formalized in the stratified-spaces literature (e.g. Lurie, Higher Algebra App. A; Treumann; Ayala–Francis–Tanaka)
ideas.where_published: Not published; the general programme of tame topology and stratified structures is sketched in Esquisse d'un programme §5-6

ideas.what: Corollary 1/2: with nonempty strata, the order on I is recovered from inclusion of the closed pieces (j ≤ i ⇔ X_j ⊂ X_i ⇔ X_j° meets X_i); i ↦ X_i is an order embedding ('figure rigide').
ideas.modern_name: The stratifying poset is recovered from the closure/inclusion order of strata (frontier condition-type statement at set level)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Folklore (stratification theory: Whitney, Thom, Mather; poset-stratified spaces)

deep.surprise_reason: An elementary set-theoretic lemma on poset-indexed decompositions, routine and essentially folklore. The only point of interest is that Grothendieck himself catches a missing monotonicity hypothesis ('?!'). Nothing here is absent from the literature in a meaningful way.
transcription_corrections: The ambient set on this page is written |Φ| (Phi), consistent with |𝔓| on neighbouring pages; it is the same underlying set of the figure.
'Ceci montre donc que' reads more like 'Cela montre donc que'.
The NB ends with '?!' and a large '??' above X_j, signalling Grothendieck's own doubt about the missing monotonicity hypothesis.
In the Corollary 1 chain, the last term is (X_j° ∩ X_i ≠ ∅), with a heavy overwritten correction of the index to i.

The margin note reads roughly: 'Attention: on n'a en général pas (iv) sans la condition X_j° ≠ ∅, car la condition X_j° ⊂ X_i ⇒ j ≤ i (pour X_j° vide) ... alors que (i) est vérifiée'. The empty open stratum would force j ≤ i for all i.
